display.title: The Ohel Miracle
display.summary_short: Why Yidden daven at a tzaddik's Ohel, and how a businessman's prayer at the Mitteler Rebbe's Ohel came at the very moment his gravely ill wife recovered.
display.summary_long: The storyteller opens with a letter of the Rebbe answering someone who did not understand why people go to the Ohel: a tzaddik's neshamah lives on, nobody davens to the tzaddik, and he is asked to bring our tefillos to Hashem, like the head of a body. He describes how often the Rebbe went to the Ohel, and retells a story a cheder teacher told his class there: a Chassid merited a child only because he once davened Mincha under a tree where the tzaddik Reb Simcha Bunim of Peshischa had davened. Then comes a story recorded by Rabbi Yaakov Kadaner. A businessman from his town, not yet a Chassid, promises to visit the Mitteler Rebbe's Ohel in Nezhin. His trip goes badly, he loses his money, and he feels something is wrong at home. At the Ohel he cries, leaves notes for his family and for his wife's recovery, and feels sudden relief. Back home he learns his wife, whom three doctors had given up on, woke up at nine in the morning on that very day, the moment he put down his note. Along the way the storyteller teaches that a doctor may heal but must never give up hope.
display.lesson: Tzaddikim never really leave us; when we connect to them and daven at their resting place, they bring our tefillos to Hashem.

advisories.note: A wife becomes critically ill and the doctors give up hope; she recovers.
